stories.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 2
stories.summary: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's rankings are here to help.
stories.body:
Welcome to Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season and our weekly PPR fantasy football superflex rankings. We know many of you compete in superflex formats that invite/covet second quarterbacks in starting lineups, and these rankings account for that. It might look odd to see the lowest-ranked fantasy passers ahead of typical RB2 and WR2 options, but the potential scoring impact demands it.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

Jump to a section:

Superflex rankings (with QBs)

Standard flex rankings (RBs, WRs, TEs only)

-->These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Lions-Bills game.

-->

We love the 34 touches in Week 1. Keep 'em coming.

stories.headline: Man United need wins after bad week of JJ Gabriel unrest, protests and derby drama
stories.summary: Things have gone from bad to worse this week for Man United, with defeats on and off the field. Victory against Brighton in midweek would go a long way to lifting the mood.
stories.body:
Fan protests, a derby defeat with a side of injustice and their best young player asking to leave -- it's not been a great week for Manchester United.

Sunday started with around 500 supporters staging a demonstration against the club's ownership prior to the Manchester derby. As players from United and City walked out at Old Trafford, the banners in the Stretford End were replaced with just one which read: "The way you treat us is a disgrace."

The game itself ended 1-0 to City, decided by a wrongly awarded Erling Haaland goal in a match that saw United playing with a man-advantage for much of it. United received an apology from referee's body Pro Ref on Sunday evening regarding the goal, though the feeling internally was that it meant very little given it wouldn't change a damaging result.

On Monday, club bosses were keen to move past the controversy. They insisted they wanted Michael Carrick and his players to put the City game behind them and focus fully on getting back to winning ways against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. Then, on Tuesday, news broke that 15-year-old wonderkid JJ Gabriel wants to leave.

Gabriel, one of the most highly rated young players in England's academy system, was due to be in Carrick's squad against Brighton. A bright talent edging his way toward a senior career would have been a welcome good news story. Instead, the request to leave made by Gabriel and his representatives will only add to the feeling for those on the outside that things are not going well.

United are surprised by Gabriel's decision, sources tell ESPN. They're also unclear about the exact reasons behind it.

Director of football Jason Wilcox led a charm offensive in the summer of 2025 to keep hold of Gabriel, with particular emphasis given to his planned pathway to the first team. He was promoted to train with the squad under Ruben Amorim and also when Carrick took over in January. Gabriel then made his senior debut in a preseason game against Atletico Madrid in August and has been quickly bumped up to the Under-21s.

Gabriel has already scored twice in Premier League 2 this season and got a hat trick in the UEFA Youth League -- an U19 competition -- last week against Sabah FK. He was named last season's Premier League Under-18 player of the year and followed in the footsteps of Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo by claiming United's young player of the year award.

For someone who won't turn 16 until next month, his accomplishments are already about as good as one could ask for. The danger now is that Gabriel could be pried away and go on to become a superstar elsewhere. But that's something for the future and as disappointing as it is for United, there are very few immediate implications.

Eligible to make his professional debut this season, the plan was always to ease Gabriel in gently. In the summer, the expectation was that he would play the bulk of his football for the U18s and the U21s. Shea Lacey, the 19-year-old winger, is considered further along in his development and has already four Premier League appearances.

Despite Gabriel's request to leave immediately, United hope they can still turn the situation around. He's under contract until the end of the season and cannot be deregistered. He's eligible to sign scholarship forms once he turns 16 and with more than 10 months between his birthday on Oct. 6 and next summer, there's time for the club to rebuild their relationship with Gabriel and his family.

It remains uncertain, and in any event it's unlikely to happen in time to prevent Carrick from having to answer some tricky questions. His weekly news conference on Friday will be tougher to negotiate if United don't beat Brighton on Wednesday. Fans are keen for at least one cup run after losing their opening games in both the Carabao Cup and FA Cup last season.

Perhaps more importantly, Carrick needs to start chalking up some positive results after a mixed start to the new campaign. Defeat to City left United with just four points from four Premier League games to sit 13th in the table. Their record in all competitions this season is two wins from five.

While the fan protest on Sunday was focused around ticketing issues and rising prices, there's also disquiet about United's relatively subdued transfer window in comparison to the money spent by traditional rivals. There's particular worry about the defense and whether there's enough cover for left back Luke Shaw, who has missed the past two games with injury.

It doesn't get any easier for Carrick from here, either; Brighton's visit is followed by an awkward trip to Fulham, who picked up a creditable point at Liverpool at the weekend. After the extended international break, United face a tough run of three games in eight days against Tottenham, Atletico Madrid and Leeds.

Most of the outside noise tends to disappear when United are winning games. But after a difficult start to the season compounded by protests and a shock transfer request, the last thing Carrick and the club need is another bad week.

stories.headline: Cristian 'Kily' González arrives to take charge of Messi, Miami
stories.summary: New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.
stories.body:
FORT LAUDERDALE, Fla. -- New Inter Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said he feels blessed at being given the opportunity to lead the club and coach Lionel Messi, after formerly taking up the role on Tuesday.

González has now received the authorization to begin the job after being announced last month as the permanent replacement for interim coach Guillermo Hoyos on a contract through June 2028.

- Source: Colombia targeting U.S. U20 dual national Shaw

- Messi tracker: All goals, assists, key moments for Miami, Argentina in 2026

- Messi scores, but Nashville strikes late to deny Miami win

The job sees him reunite with Messi after the two shared the field for Argentina in two World Cup qualifiers in 2005.

"There are things in football that simply cannot be described in words; they are unique feelings. I feel privileged and blessed to have this opportunity and to share the fantastic relationship I have with Leo," González said in a news conference.

"I adore him, he knows it, and that makes this moment even more special. Being with him and sharing experiences with the incredible players on this squad. Honestly, as a coach, I feel completely fulfilled.

"Of course, this is all wonderful, but now we have to get to work. God willing, we'll start off strong tomorrow and win the championship."

González led his first training session with Inter Miami on Tuesday after landing in Miami from Argentina earlier in the morning. He will be on the sidelines for the team's Campeones Cup match against Liga MX champions Cruz Azul on Wednesday night at Nu Stadium.

Inter Miami reached an agreement with González on Aug. 27, but the coach could not take over for Hoyos until receiving his work permit.

"What were these past few days like? To be honest, they were filled with a lot of anticipation. It had been nearly two and a half weeks and I couldn't be here, but this unique opportunity, something I hadn't even dared to dream of, became a reality," González said.

"We spoke with the club, and they offered me the chance to join the team; I said yes immediately. Being with the players, seeing their willingness to welcome my coaching staff, and watching them train the way they did today honestly, it made me very happy and gave me a huge boost of energy for tomorrow's match."

Inter Miami currently sits in second place on the Eastern Conference table with 45 points in 25 games. The team has recorded just one victory in its last nine games.

Inter Miami forward Luis Suárez said he wants to use the game against Cruz Azul to start strong under new leadership.

"When it comes to playing a match like this, it's a final. There is no time to dwell on the past, the only thing that matters is looking ahead to tomorrow," Suárez said. "We've come through a challenging run of games, but now we face the best possible scenario: playing a final and moving forward with a new coach who brings great positive energy, a strong desire to grow and plenty of enthusiasm.

"That attitude is contagious, and we are ready to support him and his coaching staff."

Inter Miami hosts Cruz Azul before returning to Major League Soccer regular season action on Sunday against San Diego.

stories.headline: UFC's Islam Makhachev questions validity of Jon Jones' wins streak
stories.summary: UFC champ Islam Makhachev believes Jon Jones' failed drug tests and issues outside the Octagon invalidate Jones' place among the UFC's all-time streaks for consecutive wins.
stories.body:
Jon Jones and Islam Makhachev, two of the greatest fighters in UFC history, are taking shots at each other this week.

Makhachev (29-1) broke the UFC's official win streak record in August, when he defended his welterweight championship against Ian Machado Garry for his 17th consecutive win. Former middleweight champion Anderson Silva held the previous record of 16. Jones, a former light heavyweight and heavyweight champion, would argue he won 20 bouts in a row from 2010 to 2024, but his streak was interrupted by a no-contest against Daniel Cormier in 2017.

In a recent interview with a Russian news outlet, Makhachev said Jones' no-contest, which was the result of a failed drug test by the United States Anti-Doping Agency, invalidates his win streak.

"I'm not denying that Jon Jones is one of the greatest athletes in history, but he was caught doping twice," Makhachev told Ushatayka. "I think that's why his streak isn't considered valid. Because he went into a fight while on PEDs and won, that's where a new count should have started."

Jonse (28-1) was fined and suspended 15 months for testing positive for extremely trace amounts of steroid metabolites. He initially defeated Cormier in their fight in 2017, before it was later changed to a no-contest.

An independent arbitrator later stated he believed Jones unknowingly ingested the substance and that it was not performance enhancing. Jones has long pointed to that independent finding as validation of his innocence, and did so again Monday in a post directed at Makhachev.

"If you believe USADA for finding a picogram in my system, then you must believe USADA when they say it 'It was not found to be PERFORMANCE ENHANCING or INTENTIONAL,'" Jones wrote on X. "You can't have it both ways. Last I checked, my hand got raised every time I was in the Octagon since any of you can remember. Your own coach said I was 'a gift from God.' Let's not forget you've been KO'd, flatlined, went night night."

Makhachev, whose only loss came by knockout to Adriano Martins in his second UFC fight in 2015, responded to Jones the following day, and hinted at Jones's troubled legal history, both in and out of competition.

"Jon, I'm not trying to diminish your achievements in any way," Makhachev wrote on X. "But your whole life seems to be tied to breaking the rules one way or another, and somehow, you're never the one to be blamed."

stories.headline: Sophie Cunningham: I talked with Adam Silver about next WNBA commissioner
stories.summary: Sophie Cunningham has discussed the soon-to-be-vacant WNBA commissioner's job with Adam Silver after the NBA commissioner reached out to her.
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has discussed the soon-to-be-vacant WNBA commissioner's job with Adam Silver after the NBA commissioner reached out to her.

"I have talked to Adam Silver a couple times, and I think he's a great guy," Cunningham said Monday after a Fever practice during the women's FIBA World Cup break. "He was very knowledgeable and full of wisdom, and so getting to talk to him and hear his perspective of how he approaches the NBA is huge, who he's kind of looking for. I think if you want to know the real answers, you go to him.

"But I think he's going to put someone in place who really wants to take our league to another level than it's already at," Cunningham added. "Our league is booming, so why would we not [want] someone who's going to make it even more booming?"

Current commissioner Cathy Engelbert recently announced she would retire at the end of the year. Silver has a long history of speaking with players about various topics in the NBA or the WNBA, though the NBA declined to specifically address what Silver and Cunningham discussed.

Cunningham, however, was more outspoken about the traits and characteristics she wants to see in the WNBA's next leader, though she didn't share names of any possible candidates she might have in mind.

Cunningham has emerged as a polarizing player this season because of her position on transgender athletes competing in women's and girls' sports. She has not backed down from her opinion despite a backlash that has included fans of Cunningham and her stance being confronted at games.

Yet Cunningham believes the league needs a unifier.

"I think the WNBA has always been a place for people to feel safe and comfortable. I think there's all types of walks in this organization, or in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome," Cunningham said. "But I do think with that you need someone who's going to unite everybody because it can be so different. But that doesn't mean it's a bad thing. I think it makes it a lot of fun."

She also wants someone committed to helping the league continue to grow.

The WNBA has seen ticket and merchandising sales, television ratings and interest in the league soar since the Fever drafted Caitlin Clark with the No. 1 selection in 2024 even amid the many controversies about everything from whether the hard fouls that Clark has taken this season are too hard to questions about Englebert's leadership.

Engelbert's accomplishments include signing a new, richer television contract, a new collective bargaining agreement and added charter flights for teams.

Cunningham said it might be time for the league to discuss if playing games on back-to-back nights creates a better product on the court or if they could be eliminated with shorter in-season breaks -- though she noted that's part of the reason for higher salaries.

But the biggest thing Cunningham is looking for is someone who values the players.

"I really do think that you need a commissioner who is players-first, who wants a relationship with their players," Cunningham said. "I think that's so important. That doesn't mean we're always going to get along and we're always going to agree. Like, they have a job, they work for the owners, and so they're going to have to make hard decisions. But if you have that open line of communication and that respect level, I think that it just feels different. I think that is a very important piece for our new commissioner."

And regardless of the fans or the critics, Cunningham insists she wants the WNBA to continue its overall mission.

"You continue to have a growth mindset and see other people's walks of life and really get to know why they are the way they are, and I think that's truly fun," she said. "Like you are playing the best basketball, you're in the best league in the entire world and you're getting to learn so much about who you are as a human, how other people are as a human. But with all that, with all the diversity, you do need someone who's going to unite our league and have a common goal and get us all on the same page. I think that's super important."

Indiana is waiting for All-Stars Clark and Aliyah Boston and coach Stephanie White to rejoin the team. The trio was part of the United States' gold-medal-winning team in Berlin. The Fever resume play Friday at Toronto.

stories.headline: Drake Batherson signs 8-year, $86M extension with Senators
stories.summary: Senators forward Drake Batherson has signed an eight-year, $86 million extension through the 2034-35 season.
stories.body:
Ottawa Senators forward Drake Batherson has signed an eight-year, $86 million extension with the team through the 2034-35 season, it was announced Tuesday.

The deal carries an average annual value of $10.75 million per season and is the most lucrative contract in Senators history.

"Drake exemplifies what it is to be an Ottawa Senator," general manager and president of hockey operations Steve Staios said. "He was drafted and developed by our organization and has shown a commitment to wanting to be in Ottawa long term. We view him as a key part of our core group."

Batherson, 28, is only the second player in league history to increase his individual points total in seven consecutive seasons, joining Vic Stasiuk from 1953-54 to '59-60 with Detroit. Batherson had 33 goals and 38 assists in 79 games last season, and he also led the Senators with four points in four postseason games.

The Senators' previous record contract was an eight-year, $66.8 million extension signed by Tim Stutzle in September 2022.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: No stadium, no problems as Devils look to build roster
stories.summary: The Tasmania Devils chief executive has played down concerns that a contentious stadium will impact the club's ability to attract star AFL talent.
stories.body:
The Tasmania Devils believe an unfinished stadium won't hurt their prospects of luring players to the club as they prepare to announce their first batch of signings.

Speaking at Canberra's Parliament House on Tuesday, the club's chief executive Brendon Gale played down concerns surrounding the contentious Macquarie Point Stadium in Hobart.

The $1.13 billion venue won't be ready in time when the Devils' AFL and AFLW teams enter the league in 2028, and will be primed for the 2031 season.

Tasmania plans to split its home games between Hobart's Bellerive Oval and Launceston's UTAS Stadium in the first years of its AFL campaign instead.

The stadium concerns come as the club looks to land the signatures of marquee names when they are allowed to lure 18 uncontracted players from rival clubs across 2027-28.

But in a possible precursor to the challenges that lie ahead, young gun Logan Morris re-signed with Brisbane despite the Devils taking an interest in him.

Even without a state-of-the-art stadium and no Morris, Gale remains confident in their ability to recruit players to the Apple Isle.

"We have an incredible high-performance centre which is being built, and that'll be 9,000 square metres and an elite environment to come and work and realise your potential as a male or female athlete," Gale said.

"I think those things are probably more important, and I don't expect (no stadium) to have an impact on getting players at all.

"When the stadium comes along in 2031, there'll be another big sugar hit. There'll be so much anticipation, excitement again."

In the NRL, the Perth Bears have struggled to pin down a marquee player ahead of their entrance into the competition next season, while fellow expansion club PNG Chiefs have inked deals with several star names because of lucrative tax-free contracts.

Regardless, media reports have emerged the Devils will unveil their first batch of players later this month, which will be under-17 prospects, after the league allowed the team to sign a maximum of 12 under-17 athletes across 2026 and 2027.

The club's entrance is set to create another conundrum for the AFL, as it considers whether it should shorten games, as it may need to expand the number of rounds to cater for the new team.

Jack Riewoldt, a former Richmond premiership winner and Tasmanian local, said the changes were above his pay grade.

"The game continues to evolve. The rules continue to evolve to make sure not only is it safe for the players, but user experience and viewership can be at their most prevalent," he said.

stories.headline: Roosters make Walker call as half's absence laid bare
stories.summary: James Tedesco says Daly Cherry-Evans took ownership of his off night against Penrith, as the Sydney Roosters aim to knock Cronulla out of the finals.
stories.body:
James Tedesco claims it would be unfair to lay the blame for the Sydney Roosters' last-gasp finals loss to Penrith at the feet of veteran halfback Daly Cherry-Evans.

As the Roosters resisted the urge to rush Sam Walker back for Saturday's sudden-death semi-final with Cronulla, Tedesco revealed how Cherry-Evans had shouldered the blame for last Sunday's 19-12 defeat to the Panthers.

Cherry-Evans gave away a seven-tackle set in the final 10 minutes with Penrith halfback Nathan Cleary converting a field goal soon afterwards.

The 37-year-old Cherry-Evans then sprayed his own attempt wide when his side needed him to stay calm under pressure, which sent the Roosters into a sudden-death final against the Sharks.

"Straight away he accepted it, and as a team, you don't dump that all on him," Tedesco said.

"He's done that numerous times earlier in the year and nailed it in getting us where we needed to.

"But with Chez, with his experience and how comfortable he is in those situations, we have full confidence in whatever he decides to do.

"We know he's kicked a lot, but he's missed a few as well.

"I think with Chez's experience and his age, you can't hold on to those things. I think that's important for all of us."

Walker, meanwhile, has been left on ice for a further week after coach Trent Robinson had hinted the Queensland No. 7 was an outside chance of returning against Cronulla.

The 24-year-old Walker underwent ankle surgery after suffering a syndesmosis in a loss to the Dolphins last month.

"It's only been a couple of weeks, so he's probably got another week or so I'm guessing," Tedesco said.

"But he started to do some running, which is really quick after surgery, so we'll just see how he goes in progressing to give himself a chance."

Walker's absence means the Roosters will again be without one of their most dynamic threats when they face the Sharks with Robinson forced to rely on the relatively untested partnership of Cherry-Evans and Hugo Savala.

With the first-choice halves pairing of Walker and Cherry-Evans, the Roosters have scored at a tick over 26 points per game this season.

But with Savala and Cherry-Evans as a playmaking duo, Robinson's sides are scoring an average of just 16 points per game across three fixtures.

"He (Savala) has done his job and that's all we can ask, and that's why we love playing with him," Tedesco said.

"He'll do whatever it takes for the team, we love him as a person, as a player, and he's only going to keep getting better.

"I thought he was awesome. He'll be disappointed with some moments that he didn't nail, but overall, he's excited to get on the job this Saturday and play his part."

Back-rower Angus Crichton, who was a late scratching against Penrith, has been named in jersey No.17 by Robinson.

stories.headline: Expected fantasy points (xFP): 2026 leaderboard for WRs
stories.summary: xFP focuses solely on opportunity. Here are the leaders for 2026.
stories.body:
Expected fantasy points (xFP) strips away player talent and efficiency and focuses solely on opportunity.

FORP -- fantasy points over replacement player -- is the difference between a player's actual fantasy point total (FF points) and his xFP (or expected total).

Wide receiver adjustments are made as follows:

Rushing attempts: No change

Rushing yardage: Rush attempts multiplied by a rusher's expected yardage based on position and rush direction

Rushing touchdowns: Rushing xTD

Targets: No change

Receptions: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected catch rate based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving yardage: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected yardage based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving touchdowns: Receiving xTD

Two-point conversions: xTD multiplied by the league average 2-point rate

stories.headline: How the Washington Mystics went from rebuild to playoffs in two years
stories.summary: The Mystics are riding a wave of talented young players and exuberance to the WNBA playoffs.
stories.body:
WASHINGTON D.C. -- AT any given moment with the Washington Mystics, a dance party can break out. Rookies Lauren Betts and Cotie McMahon instantly start to rock when Tyler, The Creator's "Sticky" plays at practice, mouthing the lyrics as they stand on the sideline.

The next day at shootaround, it's Betts and assistant coach Barb Turner shaking to Blac Youngsta's "Booty." Kiki Iriafen, McMahon and Georgia Amoore join in when "Super Gremlin" by Kodak Black comes on. Even coach Sydney Johnson will break out his own ... unique moves after victories.

It's all fun and games the late August day before the Mystics take on the Toronto Tempo -- until someone blows a defensive assignment in practice. That's when the bass comes out of the typically mild-mannered Johnson's voice, who laments that Marina Mabrey will hit that open jumper every time.

Things have drastically changed in the past 23 months for the youthful Mystics, playoff-bound for the first time since 2023. With six first-round picks from the past two drafts and a sprinkle of veteran leadership, the lightning-quick franchise rebuild has created a playful-yet-serious vibe that just seems to fit this particularly constructed roster. There's even the nickname that would be considered derogatory if they didn't give it to themselves (think of a garden tool that rhymes with rose).

"Young h-s, we are fun," McMahon said, barely containing her laugh. "Don't take anything serious unless we're on the court. This is an amazing group of girls. This is honestly like daycare, you know. We come here for the day, work out, have fun. Then we go back home and it's like, oh, so boring.

"The coaches had to adjust to us. They had to figure out how to deal with us and how to handle us. Some of the things we say, they can't do anything but laugh."

Shakira Austin, an elder stateswoman at 26, added, "Them girls, they crazy."

The girls might be crazy, but they've already become the youngest playoff team in WNBA history just two years into a rebuild that began before the 2025 season. Mike Thibault, at the time the winningest coach in league history, was fired as general manager and his son Eric was let go as coach. The two had been with the organization since 2013 -- Mike was coach for 10 seasons before being followed by Eric -- advancing to the 2018 Finals and winning the title in 2019.

Four years later, former Los Angeles Clippers GM Michael Winger was hired as the president of Monumental Basketball, which owns the Washington Wizards and Mystics. He was fairly hands-off in 2023 and 2024, primarily focused on the Wizards. That changed in 2025. The Thibaults were let go, and the proverbial house was cleaned. Austin and head of domestic scouting Shelley Patterson are, essentially, the only two remaining from the previous regime. Jamila Wideman was hired as the new GM and lasted all of one season.

As the reorganization took place on and off the court, one thing emerged: Winger would be the ultimate decision-maker, even when Wideman was on staff. The draft-and-develop strategy first employed by the Wizards was eventually tailored to fit the Mystics. But while the Wizards had the worst three-year stretch in franchise history, the Mystics' youngsters have had an immediate impact on winning.

Six first-round draft picks in the last two years produced youthful depth: a pair of All-Stars in Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen, both in their sophomore season; a rookie starting point guard in two-time all-American Georgia Amoore (she missed the 2025 season with an ACL injury). Betts, the two-time all-American and 2026 NCAA tournament Final Four Most Outstanding Player, comes off the bench. Angela Dugalic and Cotie McMahon were also first-round selections in May.

"It's not fun if everybody around you isn't having fun," Iriafen said. "Honestly, some days it feels like we're in college again. Like, we come into practice and we hang out in the locker room. Then we're like, let's go get matcha. Or on the road, we're like, oh, who wants to come to the movies with me?

"So we definitely have a chemistry off the court that has just bled into on the court."

THIS SEASON'S ROSTER almost looked very different.

Austin, the 2022 No. 3 overall pick, could have been somewhere else entirely. She signed a three-year deal worth $3.57 million offer sheet with the Toronto Tempo in free agency and was prepared to head north to the expansion franchise. Sources in Washington claim that never was going to happen -- she was a restricted free agent, and the Mystics were ready to match any offer -- but Austin, the only player remaining from the previous regime, was considering her options.

First, though, she wanted to have a conversation with Johnson. For all of 2024, the team's record was essentially an afterthought; the new coach wanted to focus on building a cultural foundation. Johnson emphasized he wanted the team to play with "joy" more than anything else -- so often that it became a running joke, as the coach would work "joy" into nearly every conversation ad nauseum.

Austin understood the rebuild ahead, but heading into her fifth season, she wanted to play for more than just joy and felt that Johnson was being a bit "timid" in Year 1.

"Do you want to just be okay with being okay, or do you want to go out there and see what the [expletive] we can do?" Austin said. "I'm just too competitive to allow us to settle, in a sense. I really had to talk with Coach.

"If they were to bring me back, I just truly wanted to be like, okay, we have enough players that we can be better than last year and we can still strive for success."

Austin wasn't alone with those feelings. Citron and Iriafen wanted more, too.

And while Johnson and the team have embraced his good-natured "girl dad" persona, they also didn't want to compete for a participation trophy. This season, the fiery side of Johnson began to appear more often. In a 32-point loss to the Atlanta Dream in early June, he had to be escorted off the court by three police officers after being ejected. Team security, three assistant coaches and Iriafen all failed to corral Johnson as he unleashed fury.

"It was really important to go into Year 2 withholding that we're going to have our joy, but we're also going to be competitive and ruthless in competition and merge those two," Johnson said. "Positive competitiveness is how I phrase it. It doesn't have to be like s---ty, crappy behavior in the sake of winning. 'The end justifies the means?' I don't believe in that.

"When our players -- Kira and Kiki and Sonia, especially -- were like, Coach, you can push us more -- all right, now we're off and running."

With their stars on board, the front office was selective about what veterans to bring in as it looked to construct the roster this offseason. They didn't want to stunt the growth of the youngsters, but if they were going to shoot for the playoffs, some experience was necessary. Michaela Onyenwere, 27, spent 2025 in Chicago, where Johnson was an assistant, so there was already a relationship and knowledge about the type of example she would be.

The organization was wary about the same things at the trade deadline and declined to make a move. But when the New York Liberty waived Betnijah Laney-Hamilton, who never found a consistent role under new coach Chris DeMarco, the Mystics pounced. The one-time All-Star, two-time all-defense selection, 2020 Most Improved Player and 2024 champion was Onyenwere's veteran when she entered the league as a rookie in New York. Onyenwere said she would be a perfect fit.

Laney-Hamilton proved that immediately. Before even being made active, she was leaning into huddles midgame and making her voice heard. Then games and a cookout were held at her home in Vegas during a road trip to face the Aces.

"What's really unique is just the energy in the environment," Laney-Hamilton said. "The environment that's been created, just the culture of the team, has been really great.

"It's just like this newfound energy. I feel like just a weight off my shoulders to just be somewhere different, be somewhere just being embraced and all the things."

THE PRACTICE SIDE of CareFirst Arena -- the building that serves as the Mystics' and G-League Capital City Go-Go's home arena and the practice facility for both teams and the Wizards -- features two full-length courts and six baskets. Center court on one side features the Wizards logo; the Mystics crest is on the other. Championship banners for both franchises are mounted against the far wall; panels above the court mimic the red and white Washington D.C. flag.

Before every Mystics practice comes individual work for each player, who is matched up with her own specific coach. On this day, Citron dribbles a basketball with one hand while dribbling a tennis ball in the other. She and assistant coach Clinton Crouch, with his trademark hoodie pulled up over his head, go through a variety of drills. Iriafen and assistant coach Barb Turner, the leading dancer among the staff, focus on footwork in the post.

Individual work with assistant coaches isn't unique, but it is a daily part of Monumental's development program. Another cornerstone has become what they call "decimal meetings." Approximately once each quarter, every player has a group session with the head coach, performance coach and representatives from the medical staff, executive staff, research & development, analytics, mental health and physical therapy. The goal is to use data to focus on each player's individual growth. They specifically track a variety of data points in and out of games to set goals on where and how to improve, then measure how that's coming along.

Iriafen, for example, wasn't happy with her progress earlier in the season, but the meetings proved that she was ahead of 2025.

"I'm just like an analytical nerd," she explained. "So, to see the numbers, I'm like, OK, maybe the eye test [felt] like this, but the numbers show you're trending in the right directions.

"Decimals have been really helpful to just have the facts in front of you. There's so many ways you can have your emotions play into things, but the facts don't lie."

The Mystics just implemented the decimal system this season, adapted from a version that the Wizards have used in previous seasons. That ended up being an advantage for the Mystics, after the structure went through trial and error with the men. Certain things worked; others didn't. Some of the metrics were evaluated and their importance adjusted.

There's a hesitancy to say the Mystics are simply mimicking the system applied by the Wizards, but there are core philosophical beliefs and standards that Winger and his staff consider vital to building successful basketball teams, so there is some crossover. On the Mystics' side, the rebuild has been quicker and the depths of the losing nowhere near as low.

"You have two franchises in the same building and a lot of the resources are shared resources," said John Thompson III, the senior vice president of Monumental Basketball. "That relates to actual physical space as well as the mental resources and capacity of the people in the building. Without a doubt, learning, watching, growing as the Wizards have gone through their version of the decimals, it made it much easier to transfer over and know exactly what we wanted to accomplish and how we wanted to accomplish and go about our player development."

The results on the court have been impressive, with the biggest difference on the defensive end. The Mystics are currently No. 3 in the league in defensive rating and No. 2 in points allowed. Last season they were ninth in both. A healthy Austin is the anchor, currently the No. 1 player in the league defending shots in the restricted area, according to Second Spectrum. Citron has grown into one of the top perimeter defenders as she guarded more shots against 2026 All-Stars than any other perimeter player in the league, according to Second Spectrum. The front office also specifically targeted bigger, stronger, more athletic players during the offseason to help things on the defensive end of the floor.

Offensively, Washington ranks No. 13 in the league (82.8 points per game), but it has beaten every playoff team at least once this season thanks to a physical, stifling defense.

"We want to be someone known for being just a team you don't want to go up against," Citron said. "Togetherness and toughness, that's our two pillars for what we want to be known as a team."

THE DANCE PARTIES might break out at any time on this team, but only one person shuts them down. Like with many teams in the league, the Mystics social media team records everyone heading to the locker room after victories. Turner is usually first in the tunnel with a side-to-side bop. But it's Johnson that goes viral. Once it was an all-out belly flop onto the locker room floor. There was a leaping fist pump with a landing on his knees. Once he stormed in making a windmill with his arms before a shake of his rear end. There was a spin with a Michael Jackson kick. He even once sprinted in with a bag of balls for a mock game of dodgeball. A side-to-side, hands-up motion with Amoore felt like an inside joke that is difficult to describe.

"He is a dad coach," Iriafen said. "He gets, in the most respectful, loving way, cringier every time. We are his kids' age, so I think it's really cool for him to like go home and be with his kids and then come to work and have like 15 daughters."

Austin added, "He does it to be goofy with the girls, and they think it's cringe half the time, but everybody loves it."

This is the balance that Johnson works to achieve. Until Laney-Hamilton was added, the Mystics were the youngest team in the league. There's an energy that comes with a roster that is barely able to legally drink alcohol. And Johnson has adapted.

"I'm just trying to fit in with this crew," Johnson said. "Why are we doing this if we can't celebrate gains, daily gains and then big moments?

"If we can't enjoy that, then it's wasted to me. So, when I see their youthful exuberance and I see them dancing or dubs in the chat or phrasing how they call themselves -- which I'm not gonna call them -- it rubs off. It's almost like they're giving me a license to join in."

That's where this Mystics team lives -- a balance between a young silliness and a seriousness on the court. Somehow, that has turned into a playoff team that's well ahead of schedule. And the party is never far away.

stories.headline: NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS urge action against threats from bettors
stories.summary: The NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, MLS and their players' unions are urging state gambling regulators to combat escalating harassment and violent threats from sports bettors.
stories.body:
The five largest American professional sports leagues and their players' unions are urging state gambling regulators to combat escalating harassment and violent threats from sports bettors.

The NFL, NBA, Major League Baseball, NHL, Major League Soccer and their respective players' unions on Tuesday sent a letter to gambling regulators in 35 states and the District of Columbia, proposing a lifetime ban from legal sportsbooks for individuals who harass or threaten professional or amateur athletes, coaches, officials, team personnel or their families.

The leagues and unions want states to establish a streamlined reporting mechanism, allowing evidence of threats to be transmitted to regulators and law enforcement. Anyone found to have violated the policy would be placed on a sportsbook exclusion list shared among states.

"Too often, individuals who lose sports bets direct threatening and harassing messages toward players, coaches, and their families via social media and in-person interactions," the leagues' letter states. "Threatening the safety of an athlete or their family members over a sports bet crosses a bright ethical and criminal line, and it is entirely unacceptable."

In May 2025, pitcher Lance McCullers, then with the Houston Astros, said he received threats on social media to "find my kids and murder them" after a rough performance against the Cincinnati Reds. An investigation by Houston police determined an intoxicated bettor overseas was behind the threats.

Four states -- Louisiana, Ohio, West Virginia and Wyoming -- already have similar policies in place, and some of the largest sportsbooks have taken steps to combat the issue. DraftKings and Fanatics partnered with Integrity Compliance 360 this summer to implement a technology that uses artificial intelligence and investigative tools to detect social media abuse and identify the people behind it.

"Threats and harassment in sports continue to escalate, threatening the safety of participants and the integrity of the ecosystem," Scott Sadin, co-founder and co-CEO of IC360, told ESPN. "True progress requires a unified response where leagues, operators, regulators and technology partners align around solutions to safeguard stakeholders across every touchpoint."

"It's just an infuriating issue," Matt King, CEO of Fanatics Betting and Gaming and a sports betting industry veteran, told ESPN in June.

Houston Rockets guard Fred VanVleet, president of the NBPA, said players are still adjusting to the new betting environment surrounding sports.

"We carry all of the burden, all of the risk and danger that comes with the association to gambling," VanVleet said in July. "It was one of those things that was just kind of thrown upon us, and I think everybody's trying to figure out how to adjust to it."

stories.headline: Max vs 100 explained: Rules, drivers, shortcuts and how Verstappen can win
stories.summary: Everything you need to know ahead of Max v 100 at Silverstone, as Max Verstappen takes on a unique new challenge.
stories.body:
In one of the most unique challenges ever faced by a Formula 1 driver, Max Verstappen is taking to Silverstone on Wednesday, where he will try to overtake 100 drivers in just 30 laps.

Verstappen first sat in a kart at the age of four and was taking part in competition by the age of seven -- but has been in Formula 1 for the past 11 years.

He's set to roll back the years and test his go-karting pedigree once more against drivers from the world of social media, TV and sport.

Here's everything you need to know about Max vs 100.

- Max vs 100: Meet the drivers racing against Red Bull's Verstappen

- Max vs 100: F1 drivers predict how Verstappen will fare racing 100 drivers

- What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records

What is Max vs 100?
Max vs 100 is a one-off go-kart race organised by Red Bull, which sees four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen attempt to beat 100 amateur drivers from around the world at Silverstone.

What does Verstappen have to do to win?
Verstappen will start from the back of the grid, with all 100 competitors ahead of him. He will have 30 laps to overtake all of them in order to win.

When a kart is overtaken by Verstappen, they are out, meaning Verstappen could win before the 30 laps are complete.

What is the 'fast lap' and how do the shortcuts work?
Anyone attempting to hold off one of the greatest Formula 1 drivers of all time will need a little bit of help, and Max vs 100 competitors will have access to a 'fast lap' once during the race.

Drivers will be able to use their 'fast lap' at any time in the first 15 laps of the race, which will enable to them to take a shortcut on the track and gain some ground back on Verstappen when he begins to close in.

However, Verstappen has one available of his own to gain time -- but he cannot use it until the last 15 laps.

How does qualifying work?
The grid order will be determined by one flying lap around the specially-designed course at Silverstone -- with just a single attempt available. Much like in Formula 1, the grid order will be determined by lap times.

Are all the karts the same?
Every kart is identical. The complete weight, including driver and kit, must reach 85kg, meaning ballast will be added to karts which do not reach the total, levelling out the field.

Who are the 100 drivers facing Verstappen?
Among the drivers taking on Verstappen are personalities from TV, social media, and sport, though no professional racing drivers are included.

The list includes streamers Pieface, Caedrel and TheDonato, ultrarunner Arda Saatçi, basketball shooting phenomenon Chris "Lethal Shooter" Matthews, and 2019 Love Island winner Amber Gill.

Verstappen will be able to communicate with the field directly during the race, offering an insight into his racing brain.

How difficult will Max vs 100 be?
Verstappen's challenge in this race will not be in terms of raw pace or lap times, where he is certain to be a cut above the rest.

The issues will come in the form of traffic -- with so many karts ahead of him and some very likely to be lapped -- and time management, as Verstappen will need to calculate where and when he is to attempt passes.

A few of the field, while not professional, are karting influencers who know how to get round a track, and will want to make the most of their opportunity to defend against a Formula 1 icon.

When and how do I watch it?
Max vs 100 is taking place on Sept. 16, and will be shown live in the UK on Disney+.

In the U.S., Max v 100 will also air on the ESPN App for Unlimited subscribers before a delayed ESPN2 broadcast later that day.

The race itself will start at 6 p.m., with the live stream beginning one hour before.

Comedian Mo Gilligan will front the coverage, which is set to include drone footage and live race data.

stories.headline: Allianz Arena to host 2028 Champions League final, Camp Nou to host in 2029
stories.summary: The Munich Football Arena and Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Champions League finals, European football's governing body confirmed Tuesday.
stories.body:
The Munich Football Arena and Barcelona's Spotify Camp Nou will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Champions League finals, European football's governing body confirmed Tuesday.

Bayern Munich's stadium -- also known as the Allianz Arena for sponsorship reasons -- held the 2025 and 2012 finals, but it will be the first time in exactly 30 years that Camp Nou has been the venue for the biggest game in European club football.

Camp Nou last hosted the final in 1999, when Manchester United famously scored two late goals to beat Bayern 2-1 to claim the second of their three European Cups.

While the 70,000-capacity Allianz Arena is ready to go, Camp Nou is still being redeveloped as part of a revamp which began in 2023.

After over two years playing away from their home stadium, Barça returned to Camp Nou last November, but work is still ongoing.

The capacity is currently capped at 62,000, with the third tier yet to be completed and the roof still to be put on.

Barça estimate that the stadium, which will eventually hold 105,000 fans, will be finished towards the end of 2027 -- or at the latest by 2028.

- Ousmane Dembélé: 'Never the chosen one,' but hard work at 'back of the class' earned Ballon d'Or

This season's Champions League final will be played at Atlético Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium.

There was also confirmation Tuesday that the Parc Olympic Lyonnais and the National Stadium of Wales in Cardiff will host the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Women's Champions League finals, respectively.

Meanwhile, the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Europa League finals will be played at the National Arena in Bucharest and the National Stadium Serbia in Belgrade.

The UEFA Conference League showpieces in the same years will take place at Juventus Stadium in Turin and the Puskás Aréna in Budapest.

Finally, the 2027 UEFA Super Cup with be played at the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam and the 2028 edition will be hosted by the Astana Arena in Astana.

stories.headline: Dolphins boss opens up on contract puzzle
stories.summary: Dolphins CEO Terry Reader is calm about the big stars set to come off contract as the club gets its salary cap in balance to cope with potential raids.
stories.body:
The Dolphins have a suite of superstars set to come off contract but CEO Terry Reader has pointed to the reasons why the club remains confident of retaining the majority.

Ahead of their preliminary final with either the Sydney Roosters or Cronulla, the Dolphins have 14 players who will become free agents on November 1, including big name backline stars Herbie Farnworth, Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow, Selwyn Cobbo and Jack Bostock.

There is a saying in the NRL "you can't keep them all" and what is often overlooked in the Dolphins case is the club will farewell backline trio Jake Averillo (Wests Tigers), Jamayne Isaako (Melbourne) and Kodi Nikorima (St George Illawarra) at season's end.

Elite prop Daniel Saifiti has medically retired and will be off the salary cap books for next year, while second-rower Oryn Keeley left mid-season for the Storm.

Farnworth, who was man of the match in the 26-16 qualifying-final win, is now regarded as the best centre in the world and has constantly been linked to a Sydney Roosters switch.

"The key thing on Herbie is that all this noise was around last year, and he re-signed as well," Reader said.

"He's given us no indication, he or his management, that he'll be going anywhere. He's focused on winning a premiership .... and in his words 'winning a World Cup with England' as well.

"There is nothing to make us think what we're hearing (about the Roosters) has got any legs."

Farnworth told AAP he will put extension talks off until the end of the season and has said on several occasions remaining a Dolphin was a priority. He has rubbished the noise around him joining the Sydney Roosters.

Dolphins players have spoken about sticking together in a strong cultural environment and taking less to constantly challenge for a premiership. On top of the five players that will be off the books in 2027, the Dolphins will elevate their development list players into the top 30 which will balance their salary cap spend.

"Herbie, along with the number of players where they've got coming off contract, are wonderful players," Reader said.

"But if you look at the players that are leaving our club this year as well and the players that are coming through to get the balance right ... we're in a position to be able to keep the majority of those players."

Reader said the figures getting thrown about with regards to Dolphins players were "exaggerated" but with the ratchet clauses from the new salary cap in 2028 onwards players would be looking at approximately an extra 20 per cent per season.

With 12 of the current playing 19 all in the top 30 during the foundation season, Reader made the point those who stay would still be well rewarded and have the opportunity to challenge for titles.

"A lot of them debuted together and the nucleus of that side have an opportunity to (win competitions)," Reader said.

"If everyone wants the most they could possibly get at a different club, then the club won't be able to match that.

"Where the salary cap's going and ratchets they're all going to be very well paid men.

"It's the value they put on playing together and staying together. Penrith have won four premierships and been a dominant club for the last six to seven years with a key nucleus.

"And that's still our intention ... that we'll be able to hold onto hopefully all of them."
